source.title: From invitation to eviction: How plants control arbuscular mycorrhizal symbiosis
source.framework: six overlapping checkpoints: invitation, admission, accommodation, investment, maintenance, termination and renewal
source.central_limit: performance-sensitive evaluation is a hypothesis; gene expression, colonization abundance or arbuscule degeneration alone do not establish resource flux or selective sanction

checkpoints.name: invitation
checkpoints.biological_question: Do host-derived cues increase fungal activity or encounter probability?

checkpoints.name: admission
checkpoints.biological_question: Does fungal signal perception support host entry competence?

checkpoints.name: accommodation
checkpoints.biological_question: Is the intracellular interface constructed and supported?

checkpoints.name: investment
checkpoints.biological_question: Are carbon/lipid investment and reciprocal resource movements measured?

checkpoints.name: maintenance
checkpoints.biological_question: Does a functioning interface persist and contribute to host nutrient acquisition?

checkpoints.name: termination_and_renewal
checkpoints.biological_question: What is the fate of this specific interface: persistence, dismantling or renewal?

design_rules: checkpoint events may overlap, recur and differ across interfaces
plant regulation is substantial but not unilateral; fungal regulatory signals are preserved
local arbuscule termination is not removal of the connected fungal individual or genotype
performance-sensitive evaluation requires measured resource contribution, host response, same-interface fate and matched control
claim_ceiling: evidence organization and claim qualification only; no established biological performance evaluation or selective sanction claim
